The slice is constructed #' around the current point `x0` using the given log-density #' function `logf`. #' #' @param x0 Numeric scalar, current state. #' @param logf Function that returns the log-density at a point. #' @param w Estimated typical slice width (default 1). #' @param lower Lower bound (default `-Inf`). #' @param upper Upper bound (default `Inf`). #' @param max_steps_out Maximum number of stepping-out steps (default 50). #' @param max_iter Maximum iterations for the shrinkage phase (default 200). #' #' @return A list with components `x` (new state) and `n_eval` #' (number of log-density evaluations). #' @export bounded_slice_update <- function(x0, logf, w = 1, lower = -Inf, upper = Inf, max_steps_out = 50, max_iter = 200) { if (upper <= lower) { return(list(x = x0, n_eval = 0)) } eps <- 1e-12 if (is.finite(lower)) x0 <- max(x0, lower + eps) if (is.finite(upper)) x0 <- min(x0, upper - eps) f0 <- logf(x0) n_eval <- 1L if (!is.finite(f0)) { return(list(x = x0, n_eval = n_eval)) } logy <- f0 + log(runif(1)) L <- x0 - runif(1) * w R <- L + w if (is.finite(lower)) L <- max(L, lower) if (is.finite(upper)) R <- min(R, upper) J <- floor(runif(1) * max_steps_out) K <- max_steps_out - 1L - J while (J > 0 && (!is.finite(lower) || L > lower)) { fL <- logf(L) n_eval <- n_eval + 1L if (!is.finite(fL) || fL <= logy) break L <- L - w if (is.finite(lower)) L <- max(L, lower) J <- J - 1L } while (K > 0 && (!is.finite(upper) || R < upper)) { fR <- logf(R) n_eval <- n_eval + 1L if (!is.finite(fR) || fR <= logy) break R <- R + w if (is.finite(upper)) R <- min(R, upper) K <- K - 1L } for (iter in seq_len(max_iter)) { x1 <- runif(1, L, R) f1 <- logf(x1) n_eval <- n_eval + 1L if (is.finite(f1) && f1 >= logy) { return(list(x = x1, n_eval = n_eval)) } if (x1 < x0) { L <- x1 } else { R <- x1 } } list(x = x0, n_eval = n_eval) } #' Full-interval slice sampler update #' #' Performs a single slice sampling step using the full interval #' `[lower, upper]` as the initial slice. Both `lower` and `upper` #' must be finite. The algorithm shrinks the interval toward the #' current point until a valid sample is found. #' #' @param x0 Numeric scalar, current state. #' @param logf Function that returns the log-density at a point. #' @param lower Finite lower bound. #' @param upper Finite upper bound. #' @param max_iter Maximum iterations for the shrinkage phase (default 200). #' #' @return A list with components `x` (new state) and `n_eval` #' (number of log-density evaluations). Gaussian process log-marginal likelihood for the #' one-dimensional model assuming a separable covariance function. #' The covariance matrix is \eqn{\sigma_\varepsilon^2(\rho^2 R + I)}, #' where \eqn{R} depends on the squared distances in `x` and `u`. #' #' @param y Numeric vector of responses. #' @param u Numeric vector, latent covariate. #' @param Dx Numeric matrix of squared distances in the `x`-space. #' @param logtheta Numeric vector of length 3: log-transformed #' \eqn{\rho}, \eqn{\theta_x}, \eqn{\theta_u}. #' @param sigma2_eps Error variance \eqn{\sigma_\varepsilon^2}. #' #' @return A list with components `loglik` (log-likelihood value), #' `R` (correlation matrix), `A` (scaled covariance matrix), #' `cholA` (Cholesky factor of `A`), `Ainv_y` (solution of `A x = y`), #'
